card.title: Band theory — why metals conduct and glass does not

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Crowded atoms split their energy levels into BANDS: filled valence band below, empty conduction band above, separated by a gap Eg. Metals have overlapping bands (free highway), insulators a ~5 eV+ chasm (no crossing), semiconductors a ~1 eV gap crossable by heat or light. Pure (intrinsic) silicon conducts feebly; doping (extrinsic) donates electrons (n-type, pentavalent) or holes (p-type, trivalent) — the entire electronics age in one paragraph.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: gap ladder: metals Eg ≈ 0 (overlap) · semiconductors Eg ~ 1 eV (Si 1.1, Ge 0.7) · insulators Eg ≳ 5 eV  ·  conductivity σ = n·e·μ (carriers × charge × mobility)  ·  holes behave as +e carriers moving opposite to electrons

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Band pictures assume crystalline periodicity (amorphous solids smear the edges). Intrinsic conduction needs enough kT to bridge Eg — at absolute zero even semiconductors insulate. Doping helps only at dilute levels (~1 in 10⁶); heavy doping turns degenerate (metallic).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Intrinsic carrier = thermally generated electron–hole pair. Forward-biased p–n junction floods carriers across (conducts); reverse bias strips them (blocks) — rectification. NEB 2022's elastic-vs-plastic 2-marker sits in this unit's bank as the odd one out — answer by deformation recovery, not bands.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Classify by gap: overlapping bands → metal (copper conducts at any T); 1.1 eV gap → silicon (conducts when heated/illuminated, dopable both ways); 9 eV gap → diamond (insulator despite being pure carbon). Same element family, three behaviours — gap size decides (NEB 2023, 5-mark pattern).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Qualitative bands predict WHO conducts, not HOW WELL (mobility needs scattering theory). The rigid-band picture strains under heavy doping and strong fields. Superconductors (zero resistance below Tc) lie completely outside band logic — Cooper pairs, not free carriers.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: N atoms → each atomic level splits into N sub-levels (Pauli), merging into quasi-continuous bands; the Fermi level marks the top filled state at 0 K. Metals: Fermi level inside a band (half-empty highway). Semiconductors: Fermi in the gap, with thermal tail n ∝ e^(−Eg/2kT) spilling carriers across — the exponential behind every thermistor.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Explain band theory + differentiate the three' is the 5-marker — draw the three band diagrams (overlap / small gap / huge gap) and the answer writes itself. n-type = pentavalent donor, p-type = trivalent acceptor; intrinsic = pure + thermal pairs.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (5): band theory + metals/insulators/semiconductors differentiation. NEB 2022 (2): intrinsic semiconductor + electrons/holes as carriers. NEB 2022 (2): elastic vs plastic body.
